prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: opaque material texture atlas for a painterly fantasy board-game map. Input images are STYLE REFERENCES ONLY; do not reproduce the board, text, icons, regions, white outlines or scenery.
Create a square 2x2 grid of FOUR FULL-BLEED square terrain-material swatches, each filling its quadrant with no gap, margin, frame, label or transparency. Each quadrant is a continuous flat terrain surface seen straight down, painted in restrained gouache/oil brushwork to match the references. This is surface material, NOT standalone cliff objects or shoreline sprites. NO horizontal bands, NO perspective horizon, NO isolated objects.
TOP LEFT: dark weathered coastal rock, charcoal and olive-brown stone, uneven fractured ledges and small natural cracks, subtle grey highlights. Continuous bedrock with rough patches. No yellow highlights.
TOP RIGHT: natural cool taupe-grey coastal sand and fine gravel, irregular mottling, scattered tiny grey pebbles partially buried, softly mixed earth pigment. Subdued neutral sandy colour, NOT yellow/gold/cream. No large rocks, no sea, no water, no grass.
BOTTOM LEFT: damp grey-brown lake bank gravel and silt, small slate stones, a little dark moss, softly mottled fine sediment; muted and earthy.
BOTTOM RIGHT: weathered cool grey alpine granite, blue-grey cracks, understated light-grey rock plates; dark enough to integrate with snowy mountain bases but no snow or bright white expanses.
Across every swatch: small irregular medium-scale painted detail, consistent overhead lighting from upper left, no strong cast shadows, no dramatic shading, no repetitive tiles or manufactured shapes. Keep the broad colour range muted: these backgrounds must support gameplay, never compete with pieces. No blue water anywhere. Opaque image: paint EVERY pixel with material. Never use checkerboard, plain background, text, grid lines, borders, foamy strokes, grassy cap or object cutouts.
usage: Opaque full-bleed material quadrants, mapped at a fixed screen scale under terrain masks; no backgrounds are removed.
